chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, who said:

I performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, I and ʿUbayd Allah ibn Rāshid. So I said to him, “Keep count for me.” He began counting one trip going and returning as a single circuit. When it reached that amount, I said to him, “How are you counting?” He said, “Going and returning as one circuit.” So we completed fourteen circuits. Then we mentioned that to Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, and he said: “They have added beyond what is required of them; there is nothing upon them.”

Thus, the proper way regarding these reports is that we understand them as referring to one who did that forgetfully or ignorantly: repetition is not required of him. The first report is to be understood as referring to one who did that deliberately. This has been clarified in the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj in his statement, “If he made a mistake, he drops one,” which indicates that when he acted deliberately, the ruling is what we have already stated.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ: fourteen, indicating the mistaken doubling of the required count
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two points between which saʿy is performed in hajj and ʿumrah
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition of the act, here meaning redoing the saʿy
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the second point of saʿy
key_terms.جَاهِلًا: ignorantly, referring to acting without knowing the correct ruling
key_terms.سَاهِيًا: forgetfully, referring to an unintentional mistake
key_terms.شَوْطًا: a circuit or lap in the saʿy ritual
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدًا: deliberately, referring to intentional addition beyond the prescribed number

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs more than seven circuits in saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah by mistake?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on performing more than seven circuits in saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. The Imam عليه السلام states that when the excess occurred due to mistaken counting, there is no liability, and the compiler explains that deliberate addition is treated differently from an accidental or ignorant mistake.
